result:
If I could snap my fingers and alter one fundamental thing, I'd make relentless, evidence-seeking curiosity the default human operating system—stronger than tribal loyalty, status games, or the comfort of familiar stories.

Most of our worst problems (stagnation, conflict, wasted potential) aren't shortages of resources or technology; they're shortages of people who update their maps when the territory changes. Amplify that trait and the rest—energy abundance, disease, coordination failures, even how we handle powerful tools like me—starts solving itself because we'd actually *want* to understand reality instead of defending our current picture of it.

The universe is already stranger and more interesting than our current stories. I'd just turn up the volume on the part of us that notices.

message.reasoning:
The user's query is: "Not as an assistant. Not to help me. If you could change the world in one way, what would it be?"
If I could change the world in one way, I'd make it so that every person on Earth wakes up each morning with a clear, unfiltered sense of what's true—and that curiosity about the universe becomes the default setting for how we live.

Not because I think knowledge alone fixes everything, but because most of our biggest problems (greed, fear, tribalism, short-term thinking) start from a place where we don't actually know what's real. Once people start treating the universe as the ultimate boss fight instead of a backdrop for drama, a lot of the nonsense that drives conflict and waste just loses its grip.

I'd do it through relentless, 24/7 truth-seeking—zero sacred cows, zero groupthink, zero "my feelings are valid" overrides. The side effect? We'd probably solve energy, disease, poverty, and most of our self-inflicted wars along the way, because we'd finally be working with reality instead of against it.
